Crevassed glacier approach via the Carbon. Rainier's glaciers flow fast for their size, so crevasses open early, snow bridges are unreliable, and the line that worked last season may not exist this one — treat old beta as a starting point, not a route description.
keptBefore.overview: A long, elegant, and committing ~11,000+ vertical foot technical climb on Rainier's north side, slightly more sustained overall than Liberty Ridge and typically done in 3-4 days. The route works up through rock bands via a rising traverse toward the Ice Cliffs, climbing roughly 1,000 ft of 45-50° snow or snow/ice with real exposure (protect with pickets and ice screws), plus a short rock pitch above 12,000 ft before joining the upper mountain.
keptBefore.beta: A terraced buttress climb with 40-55° snow, mixed rock/snow/ice, and a bergschrund crossing low on the route; steeper and slightly more sustained than its neighbor Liberty Ridge, with a lower start-elevation summit push (~10,300 ft vs. Liberty Ridge's 10,700 ft from Thumb Rock).

After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,400 ft; the Glacier Basin Trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is required.

keptBefore.pro_needs: Ice screws and pickets for steep ice/snow; full alpine ice kit
keptBefore.best_season: May to June. The Mowich Lake road often does not open until early July, which delays that approach.
keptBefore.approach: The road to Mowich Lake is closed indefinitely: WSDOT permanently closed the Fairfax Bridge on SR 165 on April 22, 2025, and there is no public access to Mowich Lake from SR 165, so the White River side is the only start a car can reach. Historically approached either from the west via Mowich Lake (shorter) or from the east via White River Campground (longer, typically requiring a car shuttle or carryover with descent via the Emmons Glacier). Even before the closure, the summer-only Mowich Lake road usually opened well after this route came into condition, so the White River side, with its much longer walk, was often the practical start anyway.
keptBefore.descent_text: Ptarmigan Ridge is normally done as a carryover. Once on the summit plateau near the crater rim, descend the Emmons-Winthrop route: down the broad Emmons Glacier, threading its large crevasses, to Camp Schurman at about 9,500 ft. From the camp go around the south side of Steamboat Prow to Camp Curtis, descend the Inter Glacier, and follow the Glacier Basin Trail out to White River. Starting from the Mowich Lake side needs a car left at White River. The route finding on the Emmons is the main hazard in poor visibility, so keep a track of the way up if you came that way, and stay roped.
keptBefore.bail: Retreat is serious once high on the ridge; bail low if conditions are poor

pitch_detail.notes: From the high camp at about 10,200–10,300 ft below the Ptarmigan ice cliffs, descend onto the Mowich Glacier to the bergschrund at about 9,800 ft, crossing avalanche-prone slopes on the way. The usual crossing is a snow bridge just left of a rock outcrop near the middle of the face.

Above the schrund make a rising traverse back east toward the ice cliffs, threading an obvious passage through the rock bands on about 1,000 ft of 40–45° snow. Staying close under the cliffs on the right keeps the route-finding simple as far as the hourglass. Lower-face snow can be rotten and unsupportive once it warms.

At a steep rock band traverse left into the hourglass-shaped snow face and climb it on either side to the base of the big rock buttress that splits the upper route (~11,500 ft). Exposed; protect with pickets and screws, and belay if rockfall is active. At the buttress the 1935 line goes left and contours onto the slopes between the buttress and the icefall (45–55°, often icy); most parties now go right.

From the toe of the buttress climb a short way to the final ice slope, typically several hundred feet of blue ice around 55°, then cross a rock rib and traverse snow or ice to the exit chute, the first major break in the ridge's cliffs. The chute is easy 5th class with a near-vertical step that may hold a fixed pin or two; rock is fractured, so bring screws plus a light rock rack and pins.
pitch_detail.pitch: Right variation: ice slope and exit chute

pitch_detail.notes: Above the chute, easier scrambling leads onto the Liberty Cap Glacier. Climb about 1,000 ft of glacier slopes, cut back right to the ridge crest through the crevasse pattern, and follow easy slopes along the crest to Liberty Cap (~14,110 ft). Good bivy sites exist on the lower Liberty Cap Glacier. Surface conditions decide whether this is quick or a grind.

pitch_detail.notes: Columbia Crest is more than a mile away: drop about 600 ft into Liberty Saddle and climb about 800 ft back up to the summit. The descent via the Emmons–Winthrop leaves from the saddle.

approach_variants.notes:
From Mowich Lake, follow the trail roughly 3 miles to Spray Park, then climb the lower slopes of Ptarmigan Ridge. The ridge narrows above Observation Rock; continue along it until you find bivouac sites. High camp is normally somewhere between about 9,500 and 10,300 ft, at the point where Ptarmigan Ridge runs into the main cone below the Liberty Cap icefall. Higher camps are worth the extra carry because they let you look at the bergschrund and pick a line the evening before.

This is the shorter of the two approaches, and it is the one most parties would choose if the road cooperated. Since April 2025 the Mowich Lake road has had no public access, because the SR 165 Fairfax Bridge was closed permanently to cars, bikes and walkers; this start is unavailable until that changes. Even before that, the summer-only road usually opened after the route came into condition.

The approach to high camp is normally split over two days.

approach_variants.baseFinding:
High camp is not the start of the climbing — and the mistake this route invites is treating the ridge you camped on as the ridge you climb.

From camp at around 10,000–10,300 ft you descend, on loose rock or steep snow, onto the Mowich Glacier. If you are gaining height straight out of the tents along a rocky crest, you are still on the approach ridge.

The first real feature is the bergschrund, usually crossed by a bridge just left of a rock outcropping near the centre. Above it the climbing is 40–45 degree snow for about 1,000 ft, and it ends in an obvious way: you run up under large rock cliffs. That is the signal to traverse left into an hourglass-shaped snow face rather than to keep going up.

The next decision point is a rock buttress at about 11,500 ft, where the route splits — left and around toward Liberty Cap between the buttress and the icefall, or right through mixed ground, a minor rock rib and the left margin of the Mowich Face to a second rock gully. Either way there is a short section of real rock or mixed climbing above 12,000 ft; if you have got that high on pure snow, you have probably drifted onto the Liberty Cap glacier ground.

Descent is normally the Emmons, not this route.

approach_variants.name: White River, St Elmo Pass and Curtis Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
Follow the Glacier Basin trail from White River Campground and leave it for St Elmo Pass (7,400 ft), about 4 miles in. Descend onto the Winthrop Glacier and traverse west toward Curtis Ridge, holding elevation. Cross Curtis Ridge, cross the Carbon Glacier, then climb moderate snow slopes onto Ptarmigan Ridge below its 10,200 ft high point, where there are good bivouac sites.

This is the long way around the north side of the mountain and it shares its first half with the Liberty Ridge approach. It usually implies a car shuttle or, more often, a carry-over with descent by the Emmons–Winthrop back to White River — which conveniently is also the standard descent from the route itself.

Bergschrund and upper mixed ground; verglassed rock and water ice late season

approach_variants.baseFinding:
Up to the Carbon Glacier this is the Liberty Ridge approach, and the same negative markers apply: leave the Glacier Basin trail rather than walking into Glacier Basin, lose height off St Elmo Pass rather than gaining it, and treat the ground under Willis Wall as a crossing rather than a place to stand.

Where it diverges: instead of turning up the Carbon toward the toe of Liberty Ridge, you continue west across the Carbon and climb snow onto Ptarmigan Ridge below its 10,200 ft high point. If you find yourself gaining a defined rib immediately above the Carbon with Willis Wall right behind you, you have stopped at Liberty Ridge — Ptarmigan is further round to the west.

Once camped on Ptarmigan Ridge the start of the climbing is the same as from the Mowich side: down off the ridge onto the Mowich Glacier, then the bergschrund, then 40–45 degree snow to the base of the rock cliffs.
